rationale: Pursue a new sourced lead from the drift instead of extending the parent's variant list. OmniPaxos decides what trim may remove from the minimum accepted index across the leader's recorded accepted indexes, while the documented contract for trimming requires that ALL nodes have decided up to that index; the witnessed drift inflates exactly those recorded accepted indexes, so after enough re-synchronizations the minimum the leader uses is no longer the cluster's true minimum content. A child question is registered for that consumption of the drifted reports, with the sources that fix how trim derives its index and what the documented requirement is, an unresolved source-only interpretation stating the narrow argument I can already give (the drift lifts the recorded values only above content, and the StopSign-adjusted decided bound keeps the plain case inside the log, so an over-trim needs the cut to land past the entries a replica still holds), and the parent's discriminator extended to name this consumer alongside the bound question.

investigations.question: Does the drifted accepted index reach the trim decision? The leader derives its trim index from the minimum of the accepted indexes it has recorded for the configuration's nodes, and those recorded values are exactly the ones the re-synchronization inflates; the documented contract instead requires that all nodes have decided the trim index. Does a drifted minimum let trim remove entries that a replica has not decided, or push the compacted index past the entries a replica still holds?
investigations.hypothesis: Once every node's recorded accepted index is inflated above its content, the minimum the leader uses exceeds the cluster's true minimum content index, so trim can accept a trim index that some replica has not decided (against the documented requirement) and can push the compacted index past that replica's entries; a later re-synchronization of such a replica would then ask the storage for a suffix starting below the compacted index, which the in-memory storage computes by subtracting the compacted index and would underflow.
investigations.discriminator: Sampling, after several reconnection rounds and a leader change so that every node's recorded accepted index exceeds its content, the leader's trim result together with the compacted index it reports and the state of a replica that has not decided that index; the decisive observations are whether trim succeeds beyond the true minimum decided index and whether any later read or re-synchronization of the affected replica panics or silently returns nothing.

knowledge.assertion: the reported accepted and decided indices drift one index per re-synchronization round

investigations.discriminator: Whether the drift is bounded by anything in the sealed configuration (a counter or storage limit, or a repair triggered by a later leader change), whether it carries into the instances started for the next configuration from the StopSign's metadata, and whether its transferred values change the trim bound a leader derives from the minimum recorded accepted index; the decisive observations would be the reported accepted and decided indices after many more rounds, the reconfiguration handoff, and a trim executed after a leader change that left every recorded accepted index inflated.

knowledge.statement: SequencePaxos::trim derives its bound from the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration, not from any decided index per node: with no explicit index it uses that minimum, with an explicit index it accepts the index when it does not exceed that minimum and otherwise reports the same minimum in the error; the recorded values are the numbers the re-synchronization path inflates.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role; reached from the public trim() with None or Some(index). Sourced from the captured snapshot; the drift of those recorded values is the witnessed consequence documented under the parent question, so the input to this derivation is not necessarily the replica's content. No execution has yet exercised trim after a drift.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account of a lead, with an explicit argument for why it is not yet settled. trim takes its bound from the minimum of the recorded accepted indexes (util.rs 186-191) and compares the requested index against it (mod.rs 141-170), while the documented contract for trimming requires all nodes to have decided the trim index (compaction.md line 4); the parent question witnesses that those recorded indexes can exceed a replica's content by one per re-synchronization, so the minimum trim trusts is not necessarily a decided bound. The narrow counter-argument that keeps this unresolved rather than asserted: in the observed single-term drift the leading node's own recorded accepted index stayed at its content (6), so the minimum stayed truthful, and the trim bound is further adjusted by the StopSign (try_trim maps an index equal to the decided index to the decided log without the StopSign), which in the observed states cancelled the drift exactly. An over-trim therefore needs a state in which every recorded accepted index exceeds the entries its node holds, which the witnessed staleleader stage comes close to but was not sampled at a trim; the storage-side consequence I can source is that MemoryStorage computes suffix reads and prefix truncations by subtracting its compacted index (memory_storage.rs 64-67, 92-107, 122-127), so a compacted index above the requested prefix would underflow there.
counterevidence: In the observed drift the leading node's recorded accepted index stayed at its content, so the minimum trim uses was still truthful.
try_trim adjusts an index equal to the decided index to the decided log without the StopSign, which cancelled the observed drift instead of over-trimming.
limitations: No execution: trim after a drift was not exercised, and no observed state had every node's recorded accepted index above its content at the moment of a trim.
The underflow hypothesis rests on reading MemoryStorage's arithmetic; other storages may behave differently and the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer.
The drift itself was exercised for three rounds only.
